Methods for Royle-Nichols fits

Source: R/fp_occu_rn-outputs.R, R/fp_occu_rn.R
fp_occu_rn-methods.Rd

print(), summary(), as_draws_df(), loo() and simulate() for fits of fp_occu_rn(). fp_sites() and fp_ppc() also accept them.

loo() computes the leave-one-site-out predictive density from the marginal log-likelihood of each site (abundance summed over 0..n_max), with the site effects integrated out (see integrate); reloo = TRUE refits fp_occu_rn() without each site with a high Pareto \(k\). simulate() keeps the design of the data (sites, covariates, occasions, recorders, which occasions were verified or confirmed) and draws new abundances \(N_i \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\lambda_i)\) and detections from the fitted model, as simulate.fp_occu() does for fp_occu(); with truth = "mean", new site effects on log abundance are drawn from a normal distribution with the posterior mean of sd_abund_site.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_rn'
loo(
  x,
  reloo = FALSE,
  k_threshold = 0.7,
  seed = NULL,
  integrate = TRUE,
  nodes = NULL,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_rn'
simulate(object, nsim = 1, seed = NULL, truth = c("mean", "posterior"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_rn'
print(x, digits = 3, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_rn'
summary(object, prob = 0.95, ...)

# S3 method for class 'fp_occu_rn'
as_draws_df(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

A fit of fp_occu_rn().

reloo

Logical. Refit the model without each site whose Pareto \(k\) exceeds k_threshold, and replace the approximate leave-one-out value of that site by the exact one. Each such site costs one fit, with the sampler settings of x. A site that is the only one with its recorder, or with a level of a factor covariate, cannot be predicted from a fit without it; it keeps its approximate value, with a warning.

k_threshold

Pareto \(k\) above which a site is refitted.

seed

Seed of the refits.

integrate

Logical. With site random effects (random_det, random_abund or random_fp), integrate each site's effects out of its log-likelihood by Gauss-Hermite quadrature before the leave-one-out computation, as loo.fp_occu() does. The default number of nodes per effect is 100 with one effect, 30 with two and 12 with three; each node of the grid costs one pass over the abundances 0..n_max, so the time grows with nodes, n_max and the number of draws. In a test with 40 sites, the log-likelihood of a site moved by at most 0.005 from 30 to 60 nodes with two effects, and by at most 0.07 (median 1e-7) from 12 to 20 nodes with three, where 20 nodes took about five times as long. Raise nodes when models are close; integrate = FALSE is quicker but gives many high Pareto \(k\).

nodes

Number of quadrature nodes for integrate, per site effect. The default, NULL, uses 100 with one site effect and 30 per effect with both (a grid of 900 nodes). With one effect and 100 nodes, the log-likelihood of a site was within 6e-4 of its value with 400 nodes in a test with 200 sites. The cost grows with the number of nodes in the grid, nodes with one effect and nodes^2 with two.

...

Not used, except by loo(), which passes them to loo::loo().

nsim

Number of datasets.

truth

Parameter values to simulate from: "mean" (default) uses the posterior means for every dataset; "posterior" uses a different random posterior draw for each dataset, which carries the uncertainty of the fit into the simulations.

digits

Digits to print.

prob

Probability mass of the equal-tailed credible intervals.

Value

print() returns x invisibly; summary() an object of class summary.fp_occu (see summary.fp_occu()); as_draws_df() the posterior draws with readable names; loo() a psis_loo object; simulate() a list of nsim elements, each with data and truth, as from simulate.fp_occu(), with the coefficients of log abundance named abund_* and the abundances N in truth.
